title: Consolidated analytics visibility service with query scopes and export-safe filters
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: Console analytics endpoints currently perform permission checks in multiple places (controller layer, query builder, and dashboard renderer), leading to inconsistent behavior across usage views, exports, and third-party dashboards. This ticket consolidates the analytics visibility and permission logic into a single backend service (Analytics Visibility Service - AVS) that exposes scope-aware, audit-friendly checks and a safe-query transformer for export endpoints. Goal: make analytics authorization deterministic, auditable, and performant for per-organization and per-role visibility, including safe exports and pagination-aware filtering.
motivation: Customers using role-restricted analytics (billing, usage, security) are seeing data leakage across views and CSV exports. Platform teams require a single contract to enforce visibility rules, simplify console code, and enable telemetry for permission-denied events. This reduces incidents, eases reviews for Private deployments, and enables feature development (role-based dashboard templates) with clear guarantees.
proposal_summary: Create a new internal microservice (Analytics Visibility Service) that: 1) centralizes evaluation of visibility scopes for org/user/role/resource combos; 2) returns a parameterized query predicate and a human-readable audit reason for logging; 3) provides a safe-export transformer to strip fields that are not allowed in exports; 4) exposes a fast in-process cache for high-frequency checks; 5) publishes single-line audit events to the observability pipeline. Implement a thin integration layer in console backend routes to call AVS before building queries.
acceptance_criteria: All console analytics endpoints call AVS and base query filters on predicates returned by AVS
Export endpoints (CSV/JSON download) pass through AVS safe-export transformer and redact forbidden columns
Audit events for permission decisions are emitted to existing analytics-logs topic with org_id, user_id, check_result, reason
Unit + integration tests cover per-role permutations (admin, viewer, billing, security) and multi-tenant scenarios
Performance: median added latency from AVS should be < 8ms with cache hit; end-to-end page load regression < 10% in ci-load tests
Feature flag control to roll back AVS integration per-org without code deploy
Security review completed and findings addressed for Private deployment compatibility
implementation_plan: Design AVS API and data contract (predicate DSL, redaction rules) - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/AVS+Design
Add prototype library in console backend to call AVS synchronously with timeout and cache
Implement AVS service with two endpoints: /authorize (returns predicate + reason) and /redact-export (returns column allowlist/denylist)
Wire audit event emission to analytics-logs Kafka topic and add schema to schema-registry (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821)
Add feature-flag gating (flags: avs.enabled, avs.experimental-export-redaction) tied to org settings store
Migrate one non-critical dashboard (Usage Overview) to AVS as canary and run in prod with sampling
Run performance tests, adjust in-process cache and TTLs, and add fallback to legacy checks on timeout
Roll out to remaining analytics routes, run full test matrix, and complete security review checklist
testing_plan: Unit tests for predicate builder and redaction logic
Integration tests: console backend -> AVS -> DB with mocked org/role datasets
E2E tests: CSV export redaction verified against role matrix
Load test: simulate 200 rps on analytics read endpoints and measure latency with and without AVS cache
Chaos test: AVS timeouts and Kafka backpressure to validate graceful fallback and error telemetry
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: AVS becomes availability bottleneck. Mitigation: in-process cache, local fallback to legacy checks on timeout, circuit breaker with SLOs
Risk: Predicate DSL mismatch causes incorrect filtering. Mitigation: exhaustive test matrix and safety-mode deny-by-default for exports
Risk: Performance regression for large orgs. Mitigation: precompute common predicates for org-wide roles and serve from fast key-value store
Risk: Export redaction missing sensitive fields. Mitigation: create strict redaction registry and require schema-level opt-in for inclusion
security_notes: AVS will require KMS access for certain sensitive rule configs in Private deployments. Ensure config sync uses signed manifests and include HSM support for audit signing. Security review ticket: SEC-2026-14 (link in Confluence).
open_questions: Should AVS predicates be expressed in raw SQL snippets, abstract predicate objects, or JSONLogic?
What is the retention policy for audit events emitted by AVS (default 90 days?)
Do we need per-field encryption flags for exports or is redaction sufficient?
